title: Site config
description: One site (a release and, later, its website): which mark, which sequences and annotations, which marked residues, which analyses, what to check against, where to write. Changing site is changing this file.

status.description: offline_pilot: outputs stay out of the repository

mark.description: a packaged profile id, or a path to a profile file

first_of.description: each protein's units from the first input that has any for it

inputs.description: role -> manifest name, or several names combined (first_of, all_of): the inputs the layers read, by the role they fill (disorder, domains, ...)

trusted_plugins.description: packages whose layers this site may load

input.description: manifest name of the table of marked residues

exclude.description: rows dropped: their residues count as other residues, like any unmarked candidate

residue_mismatch.description: a mark that is not on one of the profile's residues of the snapshot

attributes.description: columns of the marks table the website keeps for each mark: to color sites, filter them and show where they come from. Never used by a test.

label.description: its name on the page

kind.description: category: one value; list: several, split by separator; number

values.description: value -> its label on the page, in the order shown

presence_only.description: values of this attribute whose peptides, fragments and extents may not be published (pCLAP, RBDmap): the website keeps the flag at each mark, with its label from values, and never a start, an end or a sequence: rows of these kinds are left out of every website table and map row

link.description: list: a column holding each value's identifier (in the same order) and the URL it opens ({} is the identifier)

colours.description: value -> its color when sites are colored by this attribute (default: a fixed palette in the order of values)

records.description: list: value -> a URL for that source's own record of the protein ({acc}), used instead of the paper link

provenance.description: the attribute says how a mark was found (its studies, how it was localized, notes), not what it is: comparisons of marks show it as a caveat, and the first linked list of these gives the study strata

present.description: the value is whether the column holds anything: 'yes' or 'no' (name them in values); for a filter such as "changed in tumors" over a column of changes

pair_with.description: list: a second column listing one value per value of the first, in the same order; each value becomes '<value>:<its partner>' (a perturbation and its call)

control.description: filter: chips (default) or a drop-down list, for many values

left_out.description: rows kept pending: counted on neither side of a residue test (neither as marks nor as other residues), unlike exclude, which drops the row and leaves its residue among the others

items.description: rows of another table counted as marks too (the same accession and position columns)

input.description: manifest name of the table

include.description: its rows kept: every condition holds

left_out.description: its rows counted on neither side (neither marks nor other residues), as marks.left_out

add.description: further tables whose rows are marks too, appended to the marks table before it is read

tables.description: tables with several rows per mark (each experiment that measured a mark, say), kept for the website: ptmc run keeps their rows for the counted marks (marks_<name>.tsv); no test reads them. A count question (website.counts) reads them by name

input.description: manifest name of the table

key.description: how a row names its mark: a column of the marks table and the table's column holding the same value ({marks: site_id, table: site_id}), or the table's accession and position columns

id.description: the analysis column of the statistics rows

question.description: the question the card answers, in words

section.description: the Overview section it is listed under (default: the layer's)

oneOf.description: protein_sets: the table of (set, protein) pairs; input is a role of the site's inputs

where.description: protein_sets: rows kept by what another table says of one of their columns (the organism of a protein, the kind of a set): a row is kept when its column's value is the key of a row of that table that include and exclude keep; every condition must hold. On the protein column, accessions are compared as entries (an isoform counts as its entry)

input.description: a role of the site's inputs: the other table

key.description: the other table's column holding the same values

include.description: the other table's rows that count: every condition holds

exclude.description: the other table's rows that do not count

history.description: protein_sets: members named by an older (secondary) UniProt accession, brought to the snapshot's current entry through an accession history: a member that is an entry stays, one the history maps to exactly one entry becomes it, any other is dropped. Not for sets of other identifiers

input.description: a role of the site's inputs: the history table

to.description: the column of the entry each now belongs to

include.description: the history's rows read (its secondary accessions, say)

families.description: protein_sets: gather the table's sets into families by their names, with a site's own rules file (schemas/set_families.schema.json); each family holds the members of its sets, and the source still annotates every member of its table (the background, unless whole_universe)

rules.description: the rules file, relative to the site's repository (sites/data/...)

by.description: the column whose names the rules read (default: the set column)

lists.description: the rules file's lists whose families this analysis tests (default: every list)

member_when.description: rows of every protein the source tests: a protein is a member of a row's set only where these all hold; the others are the background (annotated, in no set)

oneOf.description: protein_sets: sets from a class hierarchy (PANTHER protein classes, a GO slim): each protein's classes, and the ontology that places them

input.description: role of the table giving each protein its classes

root.description: the root's id: its children are the top level

level.description: top: each protein's top-level classes; below_top: every class under the top level a protein's classes lie in or under

groups.description: level top only: group name -> its top-level class ids; every top-level class in exactly one group

unclassified.description: a set of the universe's proteins with no class at this level, under this name

oneOf.description: protein_sets: sets made by rules on a table's columns: each row goes to the set of the first rule whose conditions all hold (a rule without conditions takes every row left); the source annotates every protein of the table's rows

exclusive.description: false: a row is in the set of every rule whose conditions hold, not only the first

oneOf.description: protein_sets: one set per item, each the proteins with a unit in its roles (units) or listed in a table (table), tested against its own universe (universe_units: the proteins with a unit in those roles, e.g. those an experiment measured; default: the analysis's universe)

identifiers.description: protein_sets: the sets hold another identifier (Entrez genes, say): each of the site's proteins is mapped to it through these tables in turn, and the test counts identifiers, its universe the proteins' identifiers

input.description: a role of the site's inputs

from.description: the column holding the step before's identifier (the protein's accession, first)

to.description: the column holding the next identifier

separator.description: the to column holds lists, split here

take.description: of a list, the first item or every item

names.description: protein_sets: the sets' names; a filter here restricts the sets tested

universe.description: annotated: the proteins in at least one set; snapshot: every entry of the sequences

whole_universe.description: the background is the whole universe, not only its proteins in some set

oneOf.description: sets.each: the rows in the order the sets are listed

the order its rows are written in, the first key first (default: protein sets by ascending p, then the set's name, which also breaks every tie here; pooled residue rows by odds ratio, within-protein rows by category)

categories.description: the rows of these categories first, in this order, then the others as they were

by.description: a column of the statistics rows

ordered.description: the website keeps the classes in their own order (the layer's labels, or for protein sets the rows' order) instead of sorting them by effect, as for classes from inside a domain outwards (default: the layer's)

groups.description: headed groups of the classes on the website, in order (default: the layer's); a class in no group follows them

background.description: the statistics rows' background, in words

sub.description: the line under the figure's title

set_note.description: a protein-set question: how its sets were made (by hand, by rule), shown in the hover of a chip naming one of them

abundance.description: protein_sets: repeat each set's test within strata of a covariate (Mantel-Haenszel across its deciles)

label.description: added to the background of the stratified rows

combine.description: with identifiers: an identifier takes the highest value of the proteins that map to it

scores.description: protein_sets, for the website only: a score for each membership of a protein in a set (CD-CODE's confidence that a protein belongs to a condensate), offered as a filter of the members at or above a level; no test reads it. Members as entries and, with sets.history, brought to the snapshot's entries; a protein in a set on several rows takes its highest score

input.description: a role of the site's inputs: (set, protein, score) rows

label.description: the filter's name

levels.description: the thresholds offered (a member's score at least this)

max.description: the highest score: the options read "at least 3 of 5"

filter.description: protein_sets: the words of its control in the Filters panel

label.description: the control's name (default: its title, and whose proteins it counts)

any.description: offer marks on a protein in any of the source's sets, with these words (In any CD-CODE condensate)

sets.description: the sets the control lists: those tested, or every set of the source holding a marked protein (all)

only_in.description: residue and conditional_logit: count only the marks and candidate residues inside the IDRs ('idr') or inside the regions of an interval table ({role, kind})

covariates.description: conditional_logit: the factors of one conditional logistic regression (one stratum per protein; the marked residues against the other candidate residues of their proteins), each a yes-or-no factor from a layer's classes (is) or flags, or a number summed over a window of the sequence (window_sum)

per.description: a numeric factor's unit: its odds ratio is per this many units (default 1)

new.description: not in the site's reference: no parity check, and the website marks it new

with.description: the parameters of a layer made from them (ptmc layers lists them): regions {role, kind, window, noun, nouns, labels, help, title, question, sub, section, track}; residue_values {role, bins, classes, missing, noun, labels, help, title, question, sub, section, track}; residue_lists {flags: {flag: role}, noun, labels, help, title, question, sub, section}

proteins.description: residue: count only the marks and candidate residues of the proteins a table lists (the accessions in a column of a role's table, on the rows its conditions keep)

input.description: a role of the site's inputs

label.description: added to the pooled rows' background

marks_alone.description: residue: the marks of a protein with no other candidate residue: left out of both tests (drop), or counted in a and b of both (count), adding nothing to the within-protein odds ratio or test

labels.description: protein_sets: a set's name on the website, by its category (a residue question's labels come from its layer)

help.description: protein_sets: a set's definition, shown on hover, by its category

values.description: protein_sets, for the website only: numbers per protein shown beside the sets (website.set_views: box plots, comparisons, lists of proteins); no test reads them. Each protein's first row; members as entries

input.description: a role of the site's inputs (default: the sets' own)

protein.description: its column of accessions (default: the sets' protein column)

background.description: also every other background protein's values (for box plots and comparisons); otherwise the marked proteins' alone

hierarchy.description: protein_sets, for the website only: each set's parents (an ontology such as the Disease Ontology, whose sets already hold the members of the sets under them), so a question can be shown as its most specific sets and as a tree; no test reads it. The run keeps the parents of each tested set among the tested sets

input.description: a role of the site's inputs: one row per set

set.description: the column of set ids, as the sets table names them

parents.description: the column of each set's parent ids

root.description: the set every other set lies under (the Disease Ontology's DOID:4, disease)

link.description: protein_sets: each set's own page, a URL with {} for the set's id (https://disease-ontology.org/?id={})

background_within.description: a default for every test of the question: the within-protein row's background (default: background, each protein a stratum)

inside.description: a default for every test of the question: in the class: a residue inside a unit of this role

within.description: a default for every test of the question: with inside: or within this many residues of one

value.description: a default for every test of the question: in the class: a residue whose value (a per-residue table) passes the threshold

at_most.description: a default for every test of the question: at_most

below.description: a default for every test of the question: below

at_least.description: a default for every test of the question: at_least

above.description: a default for every test of the question: above

proteins_with.description: a default for every test of the question: candidates: only the proteins with a unit of the role(s)

covered_by.description: a default for every test of the question: candidates: only the residues inside a unit of the role(s): the measured background

outside_of.description: a default for every test of the question: candidates: only the residues outside every unit of the role(s)

with_value.description: a default for every test of the question: candidates: only the residues the per-residue table(s) give a value for

unless.description: a default for every test of the question: candidates: not the residues whose window matches the rule(s)

tests.description: a question of several tests (question.py): one row per test and method, in this order, each test its own class and its own background; BH over the question's rows

strata.description: every test again on part of its candidates (or with other parameters), test by test

counting.description: proteins_with_both (default): as every residue test; every_candidate: every candidate counts in the pooled test and the within-protein row reports those counts

kinds.description: the kind of units read from a role, where not the role's name

tracks.description: the roles a question draws on the protein map, each a row: {title, help, style, colours, kind}

candidates_from.description: a question of several tests: the candidate residues are those of the proteins with a counted mark (marks), or also of those whose only marks are left out (marks_and_left_out; the left-out marks themselves on neither side)

sizes.description: each tested set again by a number of every background protein (a column of the sets' table, member or not): marked against the others, two-sided Mann-Whitney U, BH over the sets (method mann_whitney)

value.description: the column of the sets' table

log2.description: compare log2 of the value (0 is -inf)

background.description: the background column of the rows

reference.description: a published output the rebuild must equal

statistics.description: manifest name of a statistics table

additionalProperties.description: a published table of one protein-set question's results, in its own columns (a release's supporting table, for a question its statistics table does not hold): the run checks the question's rows against it, set by set: the same sets, the same counts, and the fold enrichment, p and q as the statistics table writes them (6 significant digits)

input.description: manifest name of the table (role reference_output)

columns.description: the table's column for each value: the set's id, its marked members (a), its size in the background (M, optional), the fold enrichment, p and the Benjamini-Hochberg q

rows.description: which of the question's sets the table lists: every tested set (all), those at q <= 0.05 (enriched: the listed sets must be exactly those), or some (each listed set is checked, the others not)

tables.description: for a protein-set question (its id) whose rows the statistics table does not hold: a published table of its own to equal

excused.description: reference rows the rebuild cannot reproduce from its published inputs, each with why (a value the inputs give rounded, say): left out of the comparison and reported, never silently

background.description: a published table of each protein's other candidate residues per residue question and class (a release's denominators): the run checks protein_counts against it row by row: others_in for each class, others_total for the class named all

input.description: manifest name of the table (role reference_output)

all.description: the category that means all the protein's other candidates

website.description: the website's look and words: everything that differs between sites. Layout and behavior are the kit's.

band.description: the header band's gradient, top-left to bottom-right

accent_dark.description: the accent on the dark theme

icon.description: an SVG file, relative to the repository

art.description: the header picture: an SVG file, relative to the repository (default: a drawn protein with its marks)

examples.description: example searches shown under the search bar

features.description: parts of the page a site can switch off; each is on unless set to false

structure_3d.description: the 3D structure viewer: the protein page's 3D fold, the Show in 3D buttons and the live structure lists (default true)

highlight.description: highlighting genes and sites in the figures: the Highlight box, the pasted lists and the rings and labels in the charts (default true)

table_figures.description: the PDF, SVG and PNG buttons that every table gets beside its TSV (default true)

default_background.description: the background most questions are tested against (their `background`); the Method page states a question's background only when it differs

placeholders.description: the site's own examples inside the page's input boxes, so no gene of one site shows on another

highlight.description: genes and sites for the Highlight box's hint, comma separated: FUS, TDP-43, HNRNPA1 R218

partners.description: gene symbols for the partner network's Always include box, comma separated

motif.description: example motifs for the motif box's placeholder, comma separated: GXRG, [RK]XR, PRPR

motif_either.description: an example of alternatives (comma separated patterns) for the motif box's hint: RGG,GAR

start.description: the start panel on the Overview for a first visit and the Help page's starts (kit-help.js); without it, three starts are chosen from examples

text.description: what the site is, in a sentence or two

label.description: who or what it is for: A list of genes, A disease, One site

help.description: one line on what it shows

share.description: where the marks fall, as one bar: a question whose classes partition the marks (else the first that does), the classes to show in order (at most three are colored; the rest is 'other'), and shorter labels

findings.description: the strongest findings to draw as small bars, each linking to its question; without it, the largest effects at q <= 0.05 on at least 20 marks, one per question

class.description: the class (or protein set) of that question

protein.description: the example protein drawn as a map on the start panel: a gene or accession; without it, the protein with the most marks

fonts.description: type: CSS font stacks, and the stylesheet that serves them (default: IBM Plex Serif headings, Inter body, IBM Plex Mono)

partners.description: interaction partners on protein pages, live from STRING; leave out for no partners card

species.description: the NCBI taxon STRING files this organism under (9606 human, 4932 budding yeast, 10090 mouse)

min_score.description: the STRING score shown first (default 0.7, high confidence)

header.description: the header band: the full band (title, counts, citation line) shows on the Overview only, and a compact one (the site name, 56 px) on every other page; the search, the selection line and the tabs stay in view

compact.description: false keeps the full band on every page

overview.description: the Overview page: which questions open as cards, in which sections and order (default: every question, in the analyses' order, under its section)

draw_first.description: how many sections are drawn in full when the Overview opens; later ones are a heading and a line, drawn when opened or scrolled to (a selection draws all)

rows.description: rows a tile shows before "+N more" (default 7, as the original explorer)

about.description: one plain line under the section's heading, saying what it answers

show.description: show only the first n tiles; the others are behind a 'More' expander (all show for a selection)

more.description: the expander's words when show is set (the count follows), default 'More in <name>'

oneOf.description: an analysis id, or a count question (website.counts)

analysis.description: an analysis id, or a count question (website.counts)

summary.description: the line under the card; {top} is the strongest class, {fold} its effect

order.description: the classes' order on the tile and its question: by effect (default) or by evidence (q), for sets where a small set reaches the largest fold when every member is marked

wide.description: spans two columns where the page has room

drawing.description: the maps of the cell's card (website.cell) only: draw the cell itself on the tile; true takes the first of website.cell.drawings, a string takes the drawing of that name

views.description: one question seen several ways, a switch on its page: each view a protein-set question (the first is the card's own)

label.description: the switch's words

more.description: more sets of the same kind, tested apart, shown under the question's own behind a button

label.description: the button's words; {n} is how many sets (default: Show {n} more sets)

members.description: the sets a family question gathers (DisGeNET terms in disease families), each with its own test: a table behind a button, with a picker of families

analysis.description: the protein-set question that tests the member sets one by one
a question gathering sets into families (sets.families)

label.description: its families as a group, in the picker

of.description: the family questions whose families the member sets are grouped into

label.description: the button's words (default: Show the member sets)

none.description: the picker's words for members in no family

id_label.description: what a set's id is (UMLS CUI)

ontology.description: a question whose sets form an ontology (its analysis has hierarchy): the most specific enriched sets and, for comparison, the largest classes that are not; the whole ontology as a tree; and a table of every tested set

short.description: the short list: enriched sets of at least this many members, each left out when an enriched set under it is listed

compare.description: then the largest sets two levels below the root that are not enriched

tree.description: the tree: the classes under the root, then their sets of at least this many members

glosses.description: for a set id: a plain gloss shown after its name, and its definition for the hover

more.description: more sets of the same kind, tested apart, shown under the question's own behind a button

label.description: the button's words; {n} is how many sets (default: Show {n} more sets)

members.description: the sets a family question gathers (DisGeNET terms in disease families), each with its own test: a table behind a button, with a picker of families

analysis.description: the protein-set question that tests the member sets one by one
a question gathering sets into families (sets.families)

label.description: its families as a group, in the picker

of.description: the family questions whose families the member sets are grouped into

label.description: the button's words (default: Show the member sets)

none.description: the picker's words for members in no family

id_label.description: what a set's id is (UMLS CUI)

ontology.description: a question whose sets form an ontology (its analysis has hierarchy): the most specific enriched sets and, for comparison, the largest classes that are not; the whole ontology as a tree; and a table of every tested set

short.description: the short list: enriched sets of at least this many members, each left out when an enriched set under it is listed

compare.description: then the largest sets two levels below the root that are not enriched

tree.description: the tree: the classes under the root, then their sets of at least this many members

glosses.description: for a set id: a plain gloss shown after its name, and its definition for the hover

starting_points.description: the Overview's Starting points: proteins ranked by a count or a protein attribute, and ready-made selections

open.description: true opens the fold on arrival (examples start closed)

by.description: marks (the protein's count), or a number attribute of proteins

show.description: the figure beside each protein: {marks} or {<attribute>} placeholders (default: the ranking value)

query.description: a selection as a link's parameters: q=...&f=...

view.description: the page it opens (default: the Overview)

statistic_label.description: each tile says what its fold is against, in a few words (on by default, false hides it)

random_maps.description: example proteins at the end of the Overview, a closed fold: a few drawn at random, each end to end as one row, with a link to draw others (kit-random.js)

open.description: true opens the fold on arrival

filters.description: the Filters panel: groups, in order; each lists the questions' classes and the marks' attributes it offers (default: one group per section, then one per filterable attribute)

proteins.description: protein-level filters: attributes of proteins (proteins.attributes) or marks (the protein's count of marks)

keys.description: filters the kit's modules add, by key: d:marks (another mark within some residues), m:at and m:near (the motif finder, website.search.patterns), o:<table> (a residue of a table within some residues, website.search.nearby), b:class, b:gene and b:score (the proteins' partners, website.search.partners); a module may add others (K.filterKinds). A key whose data the site lacks is left out

stats.description: the tiles under the header (default: marks, proteins, questions, tests)

attribute.description: a list attribute of the marks: its distinct values are counted

opens.description: the question the tile opens (an analysis or a count question; default: Method's list of sources)

columns.description: residue questions shown as columns (default: the first with classes); questions with flags (motifs) show as tags beside the window

attributes.description: the attributes of the marks shown as the Sites table's columns, in order (default: every attribute colored by or linked)

short.description: per attribute, short labels of its values in the table

quick.description: the colored attributes that get a quick filter above the table (default: all of them)

site_tags.description: values of a list attribute shown as tags beside the site

label.description: the column's name after "Window ±7 · " (default: the titles of the tag analyses)

tags.description: per flags question, the order of its tags under the window and those not shown

hide.description: dropped on narrow screens: xs below 36rem, sm below 56rem

sort.description: attributes of the marks a block column sorts by (a status by its values' order, a list by how many values)

table.description: the optional columns (the Columns menu); default: the protein page's sites table's

download.description: the download's columns, in order: each a name and where its value comes from

value.description: a built-in value of the protein or the mark

attribute.description: an attribute (the Proteins page: proteins.attributes; the Sites page: marks.attributes)

labels.description: the values' labels rather than their codes

links.description: a list attribute's link column (DOIs), item by item

lookup.description: a column of the citation box's lookup table, for each value

protein.description: the Sites page: a protein attribute of the mark's protein

classes.description: the Proteins page: the protein's marks in these classes

counts.description: the Proteins page: the protein's marks (of the selection) with this value

table.description: the Sites page: a table of website.tables, its rows at the mark

column.description: the table's column, its rows' values joined

field.description: the table's column, its distinct values (lists split)

with.description: a number column written after each value (value:number)

kinds.description: the rows of these kinds only

where.description: the rows whose columns have these values

sort.description: the Sites page's first order: a column's id, and whether most or highest first; ties by gene (the kit sorts by protein otherwise)

facts.description: tiles at the top of each protein page: for a residue question, how many of the protein's marks are in some of its classes (classes required); for a protein-set question, the sets the protein is in (e.g. its disease families)

hide_in.description: cards: the tile is left out on the cards front end (its number is in a fold's header there)

items.description: a headline card: a count of the protein's marks (count: marks, of: candidates), those in some classes of a residue question (classes), the class at its marks that the site's tests favor most (best: true), those with some values of an attribute (attribute, values), or the sets of a protein-set question it is in; kind, glyph, opens (a section id) and tip make it a card that opens its section

links.description: more links on every protein page, by UniProt accession ({acc})

default_links.description: false: leave out the kit's own list (config/protein_links.json)

numbering.description: proteins numbered as papers do, in labels and links: a protein whose gene (or, without a gene, name) matches is shown at UniProt position + offset (histones without the initiator methionine: offset -1)

genes.description: a regular expression on the gene

names.description: a regular expression on the protein's name (case-insensitive), for a protein without a gene

card.description: the site card's blocks, read from the attributes and website.tables (evidence, states, changes, calls, records, writer, sources, inhibitors, cite); ptmc check names a table, attribute or column a block reads that does not exist

table.description: the protein page's sites table: its columns (the Columns menu; default: true for those shown at first) and a filter by an attribute's values

structure.description: the 3D viewer's evidence at the marks, read through website.tables (CONTRACTS.md, Structure evidence); the structures themselves are read live

contacts.description: PDB entries in which a mark touches RNA, DNA, a protein or another copy (a site_evidence table: kind, ids, partner, partner_accession)

table.description: the website.tables table that holds it (CONTRACTS.md, Tables the protein pages show)

include.description: rows kept: conditions on the format's columns

label.description: what the page calls this evidence

kinds.description: the table's kind codes mapped to the viewer's (rna, dna, protein, self; hybrid for bound)

bound.description: the RNA or DNA a mark touches in an entry (a bound_windows table: entry, kind, chain, nucleotides, numbers, distances)

table.description: the website.tables table that holds it (CONTRACTS.md, Tables the protein pages show)

include.description: rows kept: conditions on the format's columns

label.description: what the page calls this evidence

kinds.description: the table's kind codes mapped to the viewer's (rna, dna, protein, self; hybrid for bound)

predicted.description: predicted complexes at a mark (a site_evidence table: partner, partner_accession, ids as the model, score)

table.description: the website.tables table that holds it (CONTRACTS.md, Tables the protein pages show)

include.description: rows kept: conditions on the format's columns

label.description: what the page calls this evidence

background.description: a published table of each protein's other candidate residues per residue question and class (a release's denominators): the run checks protein_counts against it row by row: others_in for each class, others_total for the class named all

input.description: manifest name of the table (role reference_output)

all.description: the category that means all the protein's other candidates

attributes.description: attributes of the marks the variant adds (for example which marks are the added, lower-confidence ones)

label.description: its name on the page

kind.description: category: one value; list: several, split by separator; number

values.description: value -> its label on the page, in the order shown

link.description: list: a column holding each value's identifier (in the same order) and the URL it opens ({} is the identifier)

colours.description: value -> its color when sites are colored by this attribute (default: a fixed palette in the order of values)

records.description: list: value -> a URL for that source's own record of the protein ({acc}), used instead of the paper link

provenance.description: the attribute says how a mark was found (its studies, how it was localized, notes), not what it is: comparisons of marks show it as a caveat, and the first linked list of these gives the study strata

present.description: the value is whether the column holds anything: 'yes' or 'no' (name them in values); for a filter such as "changed in tumors" over a column of changes

pair_with.description: list: a second column listing one value per value of the first, in the same order; each value becomes '<value>:<its partner>' (a perturbation and its call)

control.description: filter: chips (default) or a drop-down list, for many values

not_compared.description: questions this variant runs but does not check against its reference, each with why (its inputs cannot rebuild it)

proteins.description: a table with one row per protein: the columns the website keeps for each marked protein (its tables, filters and starting points). Never used by a test.

attributes.description: the columns kept, as marks.attributes: name -> {column, label, kind, ...}

in_text.description: its name inside a sentence (default: the name, lower case)

part.description: the part of the kit's drawings it colors

also.description: parts it colors when they have no row of their own

sets.description: compartments: the set in each map, by its analysis

pdb_contacts.description: false: no rows of PDB interface residues (PDBe-KB, live)
